title: Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man)
summary: NH responds to Bald Omni Man's claim that giant sets hurt strength and hypertrophy performance. He argues that strength and hypertrophy are different pursuits: bodybuilding is about building quality tonnage across many lifts. Well-designed giant sets open with a heavy compound and pair it with unrelated isolations, so they save time and build work capacity without hurting performance. He also corrects how Brian Alsruhe's method was described and urges viewers to test both approaches.
claims: Strength and hypertrophy are different pursuits; people have been convinced strength equals size, and training like a strength athlete for size makes as little sense as the reverse
Giant sets are not circuits: walk normally between exercises; if you get out of breath, your cardio is poor, the pace is too fast or the exercises are badly chosen
A giant set should be limited by muscular endurance, never cardiovascular endurance
Time is a bodybuilder's most valuable resource; performance in bodybuilding means accumulating as much quality tonnage as possible as quickly as possible
Squats followed by kettlebell swings, windshield wipers and calves is a bad giant set because it pre-fatigues the muscles the squat needs
Pair a squat with unrelated muscles such as curls and rear-delt isolation; they do not hurt squat performance
He never giant sets heavy deadlifts or squats; at most he supersets them with neck or calves
In his programming strength work is roughly 20% of a bodybuilder's tonnage and is protected; the other 80% can be supersetted
Giant sets with a knee flexion or hip hinge use gentle, low-cardio follow-ups; upper-body giant sets can include more demanding moves like ab work
Bodybuilding is an endurance sport: you must be able to do many reps, recover, and repeat
Giant sets build muscular work capacity like nothing else, which is what allows more volume and growth
He uses supersets in his novice program to build work capacity
Putting all your eggs in the compound basket to get stronger leaves many people with poor physiques: the Starting Strength problem
If progressive overload means only more weight on the bar, building a good physique will be hard
Strength training pushes single lifts as far as possible; bodybuilding accumulates tonnage across many lifts, so you progress on more lifts but more slowly
Treat accessories as priorities, as Basement Bodybuilding says; giant sets exist to give isolation work its place
Never giant set several heavy compounds in a row; giant-setting lower-body movements together is a bad idea
Brian Alsruhe's giant sets usually go explosive movement, main mover, core, then conditioning; he popularised row plus bench
Alsruhe's Dark Horse template, as a skeleton, beats 90% of bodybuilding programs; NH's own programming comes from it
An explosive opener like a kettlebell swing done short of failure potentiates the main lift rather than fatiguing it; a leg curl opener is real work that hurts the lift
His giant set rule: open with the heavy compound needing the most nerve and muscle activation, then scale down in intensity
With full rest after the giant set, e.g. 4 minutes, a press is as fresh as when done alone; expect one to two weeks of adaptation
Example giant set: dumbbell press, then skull crushers for the long head, then abs or forearms
Beginners do not need giant sets beyond push-ups, abs and calves; the more advanced you get, the more essential they become
Resting three minutes after a set of curls is pointless; without supersets an advanced program would take five hours
If a lift must be pristine, do not superset it; losing a rep on rear delts is worth the extra total tonnage
Without supersets you cannot fit abs, forearms, neck, calves, biceps and triceps long head into a program
Follow influencers whose goals match yours: for strength, Alpha Destiny or Bald Omni Man; for size, pure bodybuilders like him, GVS or Basement Bodybuilding
Try both approaches yourself and keep what works; following influencers without lifting is wasting your life
exercises: pairs with dumbbell press without hurting it
